THE DAILY METALS PULSE ⚡
Weekend Edition | November 15, 2026
#Uranium #Silver #Gold #Copper 

Trade talks. Renewed Gulf tensions. A major test for the AI investment story. Next week brings plenty for metals investors to digest.

🌍 THE WEEKEND DEVELOPMENTS

China confirmed fresh U.S.–China tariff discussions ahead of Thursday’s expected Trump–Xi meeting. No agreement announced yet. For industrial metals, actual tariff relief could matter far more than diplomatic headlines.

Meanwhile, Sunday brought Iranian drone attacks on Bahrain and renewed pressure around key shipping routes. My read: watch oil closely. Another jump could complicate the inflation outlook and the opening move in precious metals.

☢️ URANIUM — FUEL COMMITMENTS MATTER

A significant late-week development: Oklo signed definitive agreements with Centrus for HALEU sufficient to power up to five Aurora reactors for multiple years, with deliveries starting in 2029. Prepayments will help fund enrichment expansion.

My takeaway: nuclear ambitions are increasingly translating into funded fuel commitments.

🥈 SILVER — THE DEFICIT NEEDS CONTEXT

The Silver Institute’s latest outlook forecasts a sixth consecutive annual deficit: 35 million ounces in 2026. But total demand is expected to fall 5%, with solar thrifting and substitution weighing on consumption.

Industrial demand outside solar is forecast to grow 4.5%. A mixed picture, and a reminder that deficits alone don’t guarantee rising prices.

🥇 GOLD — INFLATION ISN’T AUTOMATICALLY BULLISH

Friday’s U.S. PPI rose 0.3% monthly and 6.5% annually. Gold’s difficult week showed how expectations of higher interest rates can overwhelm inflation-hedge demand. I’m watching whether yields and the dollar ease enough to give bullion breathing room.

🔌 COPPER — WEAK SENTIMENT, TIGHT PHYSICAL SUPPLY

AI investment worries weighed on copper, yet Shanghai exchange inventories fell another 18.3% last week and import premiums hit a record.

That divergence deserves attention: falling prices alongside shrinking available stocks.

📅 NEXT WEEK: NOVEMBER 16–20

• MON: China’s industrial production, retail sales and investment data. This is an early demand check.
• TUE: U.S. retail sales and industrial production, followed by Nvidia earnings—a test for growth and AI infrastructure expectations.
• WED: Fed minutes: watch the debate over inflation and further tightening.
• THU: Expected Trump–Xi meeting. Tariffs and trade developments could move sentiment quickly.

My focus: whether improving trade prospects and physical demand can overcome pressure from interest rates.

Follow :  for the next Metals Pulse.

tweets.text:
There’s a growing narrative that $NVDA has downside because $MU trades at 4x CY27 earnings vs 10x for NVIDIA.

Both are hardware companies that have surged on AI infrastructure spending.

But this view misses two key points:

1. Upcoming growth: Street expects Micron’s earnings to grow 18% in CY27 vs 68% for Nvidia. Even if Micron reaches 30% growth and tighter Asia restrictions slow Nvidia to 45%, Nvidia would still be growing 50% faster.

2. The businesses are fundamentally different: Micron operates largely in a cyclical, commodity memory market, while Nvidia’s proprietary GPUs and CUDA software create stronger competitive moat.

tweets.text:
Jason on the leaked intelligence memo that led to Jensen’s resignation: “The leak is coming from within the administration”

“Who benefits from America's champion in super intelligence getting ankled?

The partners, the employees, the shareholders, they're all losers here.

So who's the leaker of this document?

It can't be the competitors, it's not the shareholders, obviously, and I don't think it's China.

That leaves, I think, maybe the people who are the decels here. That also seems a bit farcical that Anthropic or the decels would try to consolidate power on this because they need the chips as well.

And I think that's where there's something going on in the White House between warring factions of who wants China to get no chips, the China hawks, and maybe the people who want to cool off the relationship with China and make it more productive.

I think at the end of the day, we're going to find the leak is coming from within the house.”

tweets.text:
The more I hang out with top AI researchers, the more I realize how many of them are exploring architectures beyond the standard Transformer.

JEPA, diffusion models, Mamba, state-space models, etc. So many radically different approaches being explored in parallel.

It seems almost inconceivable that we won’t see a major architectural breakthrough.

And by breakthrough, I mean something that delivers better frontier intelligence with significantly less training compute.

That doesn’t mean we’ll use less compute overall. Quite the opposite, total compute consumption will keep growing. But we’ll get much better performance for every unit of compute spent.
